title: Low-Degree Hardness Precludes Eigenvalue Verification while Preserving Eigenvector Detection in a Haskell Balanced Search Index
topic: Low-degree hardness rules out eigenvalue tests but not eigenvector tests
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We investigate the impact of low-degree hardness on spectral verification within a purely functional balanced search index implemented in Haskell. The core routine performs exact rational arithmetic to test whether a given vector is an eigenvector of a square matrix, returning the corresponding eigenvalue when it exists. While low-degree tests render eigenvalue determination infeasible, the algorithm retains linear-time eigenvector verification by exploiting the structure of the matrix--vector product. We formally prove that the height-balanced invariant of the search tree guarantees $O(\log N)$ search and insertion, and we provide a static abstract-syntax-tree (AST) profile that confirms the theoretical bounds. No empirical runtime measurements were conducted; the evaluation relies solely on static analysis and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261127_170113_low-degree_hardness_rules_out}
